//: Template: copy to .stylelintrc.json in the plugin folder and fill in the
points below (codebase-standards, profiles/typescript/README.md, section
'CSS-lint voor een Obsidian-plugin').
1. browsers — three floors, one per runtime the plugin actually lands in.
Set them from where your plugin runs, not from manifest.json.
- electron: the OLDEST desktop installer still plausibly in the field,
NOT the Electron matching minAppVersion. Obsidian's Chromium ships
with the installer, which does not auto-update; only the app version
does. That is why Obsidian shows an app version and an installer
version side by side in Show debug info.
- ios_saf: the WKWebView, which is tied to the OS and cannot be updated
on its own. This is the binding floor for a plugin that is not
isDesktopOnly. Set it to Obsidian mobile's own iOS requirement.
- and_chr: the Android System WebView, which updates through the Play
Store independently of the OS, so it is effectively current and never
the binding floor. Residual risk: a device with no Play Services.
Drop the two mobile entries ONLY if manifest.json says isDesktopOnly.
remarkable-round-trip has isDesktopOnly: false (PRD N7, platform
parity desktop/mobile), so both mobile floors stay in.
2. ignore — features that cannot bite, each with the reason. css3-cursors-grab
and css-resize are pointer-only: a touch device has no cursor and no
resize handle, so they degrade to nothing. Add css-overflow here too if
you lower the iOS floor below 16, but only while you use neither
`overflow: clip` nor `overlay` — check before you add it.
3. property-no-vendor-prefix is OFF, and that is deliberate. The rule is
browser-blind: it flags every -webkit- prefix on principle, without
consulting browserslist. For a plugin that runs in WKWebView its advice
is wrong by construction — `user-select` still requires the prefix on
every Safari version, 26.x included. Worse, no-unsupported-browser-features
does NOT catch the removal (measured), so the two rules together form a
trap: one tells you to drop the fallback, the other cannot tell you it
mattered. Turn this rule back on only in an isDesktopOnly plugin.
4. declaration-block-no-duplicate-properties allows a consecutive pair with
different values, so a prefix or unit fallback does not warn.
5. selector-class-pattern — dropped here: remarkable-round-trip ships no
own styling (styles.css is a placeholder comment), so there are no
classes and no BEM modifiers to widen the pattern for. Add the widened
pattern back if the plugin ever grows its own CSS classes.
6. no-duplicate-selectors — turned back on. The shared config disables it
for theme CSS; in plugin CSS a duplicate selector is dead code.
